title: Mirzapur: The Movie Opens Today With 90,000 Tickets Sold, Eyes Rs 30 Crore Debut
excerpt: India's first OTT-to-theatrical franchise film has sold 90,000 advance tickets in top cinema chains, with industry insiders projecting a Rs 100 crore opening weekend.
body:
• Mirzapur: The Movie, releasing in theaters on September 4, has sold over 90,000 advance tickets in PVR Inox and Cinepolis chains as of Thursday evening, with pre-sales expected to close around 130,000 tickets.
  • Industry trackers project a Rs 30 crore opening day and a Rs 100 crore opening weekend — historic numbers for a film derived from a web series and without traditional Bollywood star power.
  • Advance booking revenue has crossed Rs 12.54 crore including blocked seats, with Delhi leading at Rs 2.27 crore followed by Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
  • The film marks India's first major OTT-to-theatrical franchise transition, testing whether streaming audiences will pay for tickets.

Mirzapur: The Movie opens in theaters across India on Friday with advance bookings that would make most Bollywood tentpoles envious. As of Thursday at 4:30 PM, the film had sold 90,000 tickets across PVR Inox and Cinepolis — the country's top national cinema chains — and was headed toward closing pre-sales at around 130,000 tickets, according to Bollywood Hungama.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5vMWZhHPlaw

The numbers are remarkable for a film without traditional marquee stars or a hit song. Industry insiders are projecting an opening day of around Rs 30 crore and a first weekend touching Rs 100 crore, a figure that would be historic for any OTT-derived property.

From Streaming to the Big Screen

The film is the first Indian franchise to make the leap from a streaming series to a full theatrical release. Based on the cult Amazon Prime Video series that ran for three seasons, it brings back the original cast: Pankaj Tripathi as the menacing Kaleen Bhaiya, Ali Fazal as Guddu Pandit, Divyenndu as the volatile Munna Tripathi, along with Rasika Dugal, Shweta Tripathi, Shriya Pilgaonkar, and Harshita Gaur. New additions include Jitendra Kumar, Ravi Kishan, Sonal Chauhan, and Sushant Singh.

"Whenever a performance or art form is experienced communally, the impact changes entirely. While Mirzapur used to be a 'leave me alone' kind of watch, it's now in 'party mode.' The world is the same, the characters are the same, but the story is new, and the experience is much grander."

— Pankaj Tripathi, actor

Directed by Gurmmeet Singh and written by Puneet Krishna, the film is produced by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani's Excel Entertainment in association with Amazon MGM Studios. It received its CBFC certification with reportedly minimal modifications, allowing the makers to retain the raw, unfiltered tone that defined the series.

Booking Numbers Tell the Story

The advance booking trajectory has been steep. By September 1, the film had sold 30,000 tickets in national chains. That number hit 55,000 by September 2 and surged to 90,000 by Thursday afternoon, according to tracking data from Pinkvilla and Bollywood Hungama.

According to Sacnilk data, advance booking revenue stands at Rs 9.18 crore excluding blocked seats — Rs 12.54 crore with them included. Delhi leads the market at Rs 2.27 crore, followed by Uttar Pradesh at Rs 1.85 crore and Maharashtra at Rs 1.84 crore. The Hindi version accounts for nearly all bookings, with a small Telugu-dubbed release contributing around Rs 3.84 lakh.

Pinkvilla's prediction places the opening day at Rs 24 crore net, with a range of Rs 21–26 crore. Bollywood Hungama's more bullish estimate puts it at Rs 30 crore, noting that advances are tracking above Awarapan 2's Independence Day numbers of 120,000 tickets in national chains.

A Test Case for Indian Entertainment

The film's performance will be closely watched as a proof of concept for the Indian entertainment industry. If Mirzapur succeeds at the box office, it could open the door for other streaming properties — Sacred Games, Panchayat, The Family Man — to make similar theatrical transitions.

The estimated production budget stands at around Rs 250 crore, according to NDTV, though the makers have not confirmed this figure. Pankaj Tripathi commands the highest reported fee at approximately Rs 15 crore, followed by Ali Fazal at Rs 4 crore and Divyenndu at Rs 3 crore.

What's Next

All eyes are on the opening day numbers and, more critically, the word-of-mouth that will determine whether the film sustains momentum through its first week. Inside reports on the film's content are described as strong, which is a positive sign for holding screens. An OTT premiere date on Amazon Prime Video has not been announced, meaning the theatrical window remains exclusive for now.
